_comment: Exceptions to the productive -ize/-ise regex rule engine in spelling_tool.py. 'always_ise_base' are base infinitives that end in -ise in BOTH US and UK English (there is no -ize form) -- expanded at load time into inflected forms via the silent-e rule (advise -> advise/advised/advises/advising). 'invariant_words' are literal forms (already inflected, or non-verbs) that must never be treated as a US/UK variant even though they end in -ize/-ise. Words ending in '-wise' (otherwise, likewise, elementwise, componentwise, pairwise, columnwise, rowwise...) are excluded generically by spelling_tool.py itself (any match whose stem ends in 'w' is skipped), not listed here.
_analyses_note: analyses/paralyses/catalyses/dialyses/hydrolyses/electrolyses are the Greek -sis/-ses noun plurals (analysis->analyses, identical spelling in US and UK), which collide with the UK 3rd-person-singular verb form of analyse/paralyse/catalyse/dialyse/hydrolyse/electrolyse ('it analyses the data'). The noun-plural sense dominates in scientific prose, so these are treated as invariant (never flagged/converted) rather than risking corrupting a correct plural noun.
